key_insight: A foundation-model-based temporal scorer can identify the best ultrasound frame for ONSD measurement by learning from sparse, softly weighted labels around expert-selected key frames.
clinical_relevance: This could make optic nerve sheath diameter assessment more accessible and consistent in low-resource settings by reducing dependence on highly skilled manual frame selection.
method: Extract per-frame embeddings from an ultrasound foundation model (USFM).
Train a lightweight temporal head with Gaussian soft labels around labeled key frames.
Rank frames in each video and select the top-scoring frame for ONSD assessment.
evidence_signal: Evaluated with subject-level cross-validation on 18 subjects and 323 ultrasound videos across nine sweep types, the model found an optimal frame in 82.2% of sweeps versus 49.2% for the strongest training-free baseline and 71.9% for hard-label classification.
watch_item: Performance depends on having representative ultrasound acquisition data, and results may not generalize without validation across devices, operators, and patient populations.
paper_title: Soft Temporal Scoring Using a Foundation Model: Optimal Frame Selection for Improved ONSD Measurement in Ultrasound Videos
